one_star_reviews.text:
I came in today, 17/8, at around 3pm to get some water flavouring drops. As I was looking at the drops, a young man was stocking the fridge right next to them and literally sighed and said, "Which one do you want?..." in the rudest tone I've ever heard from a retail worker. His back was turned to me, mind you. He just assumed I wanted a drink, and even then, the way he went about it was just so rude and almost like I was an inconvenience for being in the store.

I said, "Excuse me?" because I was genuinely shocked that someone could have such a tone in a retail setting. He turned around and apologised when he saw I wasn't there for the drinks.

Regardless, they lost the sale. It left a poor taste in my mouth, and I walked out.

The turnover rate at this place compared to Nutrition Warehouse downstairs is WILD. It's a new flavour of the week every time I come into the store, whereas at Nutrition Warehouse, you actually have the same group of workers there, always eager to help you out.

Most of the time I come into the store, the workers are on their phones, and when they realise you're not there to buy out the entire store, they basically give up on trying to help you. I'm assuming it's because the sale doesn't reach their KPIs.

I like that Elite Supps provides more niche products, which is awesome and the main reason I shop there on occasion, but man, is the staff there disappointing.

Extremely disappointed with my experience at Star Car Wash Blackburn. I specifically opted for the Platinum Wash, expecting a thorough and high-quality clean, but the result was nowhere near what I expected for a premium service.

As you can see from the photos, food, crumbs and dirt were still left under the seats and on the carpet, the cup holders and centre console were still dirty, interior panels had visible marks and grime, and even the wheels were not properly cleaned.

When a customer pays for a Platinum Wash, these basic areas should not be left in this condition. It honestly looks like the car was cleaned in a rush, with several areas completely missed.

I paid extra specifically to have the car cleaned properly, and having to clean these areas myself afterwards completely defeats the purpose of choosing their premium package.

Very poor attention to detail and definitely not the standard you would expect from a Platinum Wash. Extremely disappointing and not worth the money.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointed with the communication and service from Shoreline Freighters.
We were never informed that we needed to call and book a specific delivery time. We were given a delivery date, and when we called to find out what was happening, we were then told that we had to book in a delivery time. We did this and were told the delivery would be today between 10am and 12pm.
We had to change our work schedules around to be available for the delivery, only for 2pm to come around with no delivery and no communication whatsoever. We had to call ourselves to find out what was happening, only to be told that the truck was having issues. We completely understand that unexpected problems can happen, but communication with customers is extremely important.
We were then told that the supervisor had apparently never told the driver that our delivery had been booked in — despite us specifically arranging the delivery time.
What makes it even more frustrating is that we live only 10 minutes down the road from the freight company, yet a delivery booked for between 10am and 12pm has taken up the entire day, and we've had to keep chasing them for updates.
We understand delays and unexpected issues can happen, but when customers have changed their work schedules to accommodate a delivery, the least you expect is to be kept informed.
Very poor communication, organisation and customer service.
Tried to call the number listed and it's not connected? How hard is it to update a phone number.

one_star_reviews.text:
I took my 1yr cavoodle to Pawprints Emergency Vet after he vomited up something concerning, and I was worried about an obstruction. After waiting around four hours, we were finally seen. I was told he was dehydrated (not surprising considering how long we waited) and could still have an obstruction, with the only treatment option presented being an overnight stay with bloods, fluids, ultrasound and X-rays costing approximately $4,000.

When I explained I wanted a lower-cost treatment plan, I was told to consider surrendering my dog or euthanising him if I couldn’t afford basic care. I was also told that if I signed an AMA and didn’t return the next day for another consult, the RSPCA would be contacted and I could be reported for neglect.

I took him home, monitored him closely and contacted another vet the following morning, who advised me to continue monitoring him and see his regular vet on Monday. He remained completely normal through Sunday—eating, drinking and passing stools normally. The RSPCA later attended my home and were lovely and more than satisfied with my care.

I understand emergency treatment can be expensive. What I don’t accept is being judged, pressured and threatened with surrender, euthanasia and the RSPCA simply because I wouldn’t pay for a $4,000 treatment plan on a whim. I went there for help when I was worried about my dog and left feeling completely traumatised by the way I was treated.

Very disappointed, would not recommend.

I booked my car in for 12pm because I had a birthday to attend at 2pm. Their website stated the service would take approximately 75 minutes, so I booked based on that timeframe and expected my car to be ready around 1:15pm.

When I arrived, I was told it would actually take around 2 hours. I had already paid, so at that point after having driven all that way I didn’t have much choice but to leave the car with them.

I came back down at 1:50pm and was told they only had about 10 minutes left and that it was basically just the outside that needed finishing. That turned out not to be true. They were only just properly starting on my car, the mats weren’t even taken out to be pressure washed until around 1:55pm. When they got put back in the car the mats were still dripping wet. I had to ask one of the guys to please dry them but even then it was just a slight wipe with a cloth.

In the end, they had four people rushing to finish the car and I didn’t get it back until around 2:15pm. I had waited over two hours, yet from what I could see, less than 30 minutes was actually spent cleaning the car.

I paid $95 for what ultimately felt like a very rushed job. Even worse, I noticed marks/abrasions on the car afterwards that I know were not there beforehand. When I raised it with them, I was simply told the car was already like that, which I strongly disagree with. I’m not sure what they use to wipe but it’s really abrasive.

Had I known from the beginning that they couldn’t complete the service within the advertised timeframe, I would have gone elsewhere.

For $95, I expected much better service, communication and far better care of my vehicle.Not the rushed 25min job that was completed. Unfortunately, based on my experience, I would not return or recommend them. Save your money and take your car somewhere else. I wish I’d read and listened to the reviews. So disappointed.

​PLEASE RETHINK BOOKING A SESSION WITH THIS BUSINESS

I am disappointed to be writing this negative review, as my first session with Karis while navigating PPD was fantastic. However, the way Karis conducted her business afterward was unethical and took advantage of someone in a vulnerable position.

​After my first session, we scheduled a follow-up appointment. This appointment was subsequently cancelled on the day by Karis, which I understood. I did not re-engage or reschedule an appointment with her afterward. Roughly two weeks later, I received an automated email on a Saturday advising that an appointment had been booked for me for the following Wednesday. This was an appointment I never booked, nor did I confirm that I wanted, could attend, or could afford it.

​I reached out on the Tuesday prior to the scheduled session to advise that I would not be attending, but asked to reschedule to a date and time that worked for me around my child and our financial situation. I was contacted by Tiffany, who advised there would be a cancellation fee. I voiced my concerns regarding the fairness of a cancellation charge for an appointment I never requested. She stated that because I was cancelling within 48 hours of the appointment, I would still be charged.
​I never agreed to or asked for the appointment scheduled for Wednesday.

Because the automated email was sent on a Saturday, even if I had cancelled on Monday, it still would have been within the 48-hour window. Tiffany advised that if I could attend an appointment on Thursday instead, the cancellation fee would not apply. However, this was not a feasible option for me due to other appointments for my child and the financial cost, so I advised I could not commit to Thursday.

​Tiffany said she would follow up with Karis to see whether the fee could be removed.

She then sent a follow-up email that read:
​"I have followed up with Karis as per our discussion over the phone earlier. She has agreed with the option we discussed of waiving the cancellation fee if you are able to attend the Thursday at 1pm appointment instead.

​Unfortunately, if you are unable to make either tomorrow's or Thursday's appointment, a cancellation fee will need to be charged as the cancellation is within 48 hours of your scheduled appointment.
​Given the circumstances, Karis has agreed to reduce your cancellation fee to 50 percent off what the fee would generally be. Instead of $142.50, we can offer you a fee of $71.25.

​I can also put you on the cancellation list for the 8th/9th of October as requested, and I will send you a list of future appointments booked so that you are able to cancel any you don't wish to attend in advance.
​Please let us know which option you wish to go with, and apologies for any inconvenience caused."

​Essentially, I was expected to pay a cancellation fee for an appointment I never booked, asked for, or confirmed. What this says about Karis's ethics as a psychologist speaks louder than words. My advice is to stay away from this practice. Do not give your precious time or money to someone who lacks ethics, morals, and common sense.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing experience and incredibly poor communication.

We waited months for a face-to-face paediatric appointment for my daughter. In June, I was told in writing that the “next available date will be in August” and that a specific date would be provided approximately one week beforehand. I replied confirming that August was fine, that I would wait to hear from them, and that I was happy to be placed on their cancellation list.

August arrived and I heard nothing, so I followed up myself.

Only then was I told that they had not scheduled a face-to-face clinic because there apparently weren’t enough patients wanting in-person appointments to fill a clinic day, and that there is currently no planned date for in-clinic appointments at all.

None of this was communicated when I was told to expect an August appointment.

Their subsequent response stated that it was unlikely the doctor would attend the rooms for only one or two patients because of the cost of running the clinic, and suggested telehealth instead.

I completely understand that a private practice has to make decisions about how and when it operates its clinics. What I do not accept is allowing a family to wait for months under the reasonable belief that their child will be seen in August without communicating that the appointment they were told to expect may not actually occur.

Had we been told this in June, we could have spent those months trying to find another paediatrician.

Most frustratingly, I only discovered any of this because I contacted them to ask what was happening.

For families already dealing with lengthy paediatric waitlists, losing months because of poor communication is incredibly upsetting. Based on our experience, I could not recommend this practice.

one_star_reviews.text:
We are very disappointed with our experience at this centre.

Within approximately six weeks, our child suffered two significant falls while attending the centre. Both incidents occurred at around 4:30 pm, and both resulted in injuries to almost the same area of his lower lip.

The first incident was particularly serious. Our child was taken to Perth Children’s Hospital and required surgery under general anaesthetic to repair a deep through-and-through laceration involving multiple layers of his lower lip. We were advised that the injury and resulting scar could take approximately 6–12 months to recover.

At the time, we chose to trust the centre. We understood that accidents can happen with young children, particularly after our child had recently transitioned into the Kindy room. We therefore did not pursue the matter further, believing that the centre would review what had happened and take reasonable steps to reduce the likelihood of a similar incident happening again.

Unfortunately, just over six weeks later, our child suffered another significant injury, again at around 4:30 pm and involving almost the same area of his lower lip.

What was most concerning to us was what we learned when we subsequently asked what had been done after the first serious injury. We were told that no internal investigation, formal environmental risk assessment or documented corrective action had been undertaken, because the first incident had been considered “purely an accident”.

We understand that not every accident can be prevented. Our concern is not simply that our child fell. Our concern is whether, after a serious injury requiring surgery, the circumstances were properly reviewed and whether reasonable measures were considered to reduce the risk of a similar incident happening again.

Two serious injuries involving the same child, occurring in a similar area and at almost exactly the same time of day within approximately six weeks, have significantly affected our confidence in the centre’s approach to supervision, safety and risk management.

The physical injuries have been difficult for our child, but the emotional and practical impact on our entire family has also been significant. We have had to manage hospital treatment, follow-up medical care, time away from work and changes to our child’s attendance while caring for our young family.

We have now lost confidence in the centre’s ability to provide the level of safety and risk management we expect for our child.

We sincerely hope the centre reflects on these incidents and makes meaningful improvements to its supervision, environmental safety and incident-review processes. No child or family should have to go through a similar experience.

Extremely disappointing experience — twice in a row!

I ordered from The Cheesecake Shop Byford for the second time, and unfortunately, both experiences have involved serious mistakes with my order.

The first time, the pickup time on my order was incorrect. Fortunately, I checked the receipt after getting home and noticed the mistake, so I called the store. It took around 10–15 minutes for the staff to look into the order and resolve the issue.

You would think the second experience would be better, but unfortunately, it was even worse.

For my second order, I personally went to the shop and placed the order. Given my previous experience, I specifically asked for a receipt. I was told, “Don’t worry about the receipt.” and refused to give me receipt, I trusted them.

When we arrived to collect the cake, we were told that the order was not ready. The staff then admitted that they had made a mistake and had assumed I would be coming in the evening.

Even at that point, I remained understanding. I accepted that mistakes can happen. In fact, despite everything, I praised the business in front of my guests because I did not want to create negativity during a special occasion.

Unfortunately, the situation became much worse afterward.

I had specifically ordered a pistachio cake, but I received a completely different, basic cream cake.

Naturally, I contacted the owner to explain the issue. Instead of receiving an apology or a reasonable attempt to resolve the mistake, I found myself in a heated and extremely uncomfortable conversation. I was asked to bring the cake back to the shop even though I had already provided clear photographs showing the product I had received.

Rather than feeling heard as a customer, I felt dismissed, blamed and unnecessarily pressured. What should have been a straightforward conversation about correcting an obvious mistake turned into an upsetting and stressful interaction. I was already dealing with the disappointment of receiving the wrong cake on a special occasion, and the way the complaint was handled made me feel even more harassed and distressed.

I was also told that “we do things according to our training and not like local cake makers.”

For me, good training should include more than procedures. It should include listening to customers, accepting responsibility, communicating respectfully and knowing how to apologise when something goes wrong.

I understand that mistakes happen. I am not expecting any business to be perfect. What I do expect is accountability and basic respect.

If a business makes a mistake, a simple “We’re sorry, we made an error, and we will fix it” can completely change the situation. Unfortunately, that was not my experience.

This entire situation caused me unnecessary stress and embarrassment on what was supposed to be a special and happy occasion.

Customers should never feel intimidated, blamed or harassed for raising a genuine concern about an order they paid for.

I sincerely hope the management takes this feedback seriously and understands that customer service is not only about making a product — it is also about how you treat people when something goes wrong.

Another important point is that smoking is not allowed anywhere within the complex. If you want to smoke, you have to leave the complex completely.
Sound also carries quite easily, so you can hear voices and other noises from neighbouring units. For this reason, I wouldn’t recommend this complex for families with young children or people with dogs that bark frequently.
Definitely worth considering these points carefully before purchasing here.

Absolutely ridiculous pricing and terrible customer service. A consultation should not cost that much, and charging $120 for a scan is outrageous. I went to another dentist who provided both of these services at no charge and actually gave me much better and more helpful advice about my teeth.

On top of that, I had to wait an extra 15 minutes to be seen even though there were multiple staff members standing around. At one point, there were three staff members in one room while I was still waiting. When I first walked in, there was barely any customer service or acknowledgement.

They also told me that Afterpay was available, but when it came time to pay, it was NOT offered and I had to pay the full amount upfront. If you advertise or tell customers that Afterpay is available, it should actually be available when they need to pay.

Overall, extremely overpriced, poorly organised and disappointing. I received far better service and advice elsewhere without being charged ridiculous fees. Definitely would not recommend. Will not be coming back!!!!!!!!

Konnect is a "proud family business" which means they will never be in the wrong, and will put themselves above landlords and renters alike in their drive to make as much money as they can.

In the eight months we have had the displeasure of working with them, they have neglected maintenance of my home to the point it has been uninsurable for two and a half of the last eight months, neglecting fire alarms, water leaks, and broken entry doors.
Our previous agency has always negotiated lease renewals four months ahead of time to ensure owners and tenants could make informed choices, konnect refuses to do so.

Renters received a preliminary notice to vacate instead of the renewal offered, alienating them and ruining a working relationship that had been symbiotic for the previous three years, with a small addendum at the bottom sharing that this was their standard practice, the owners had not yet been consulted, and konnect could withdraw the notice at any time.

This is a calculated move on their part, as the people hurt by the uncertainty are landlords and tenants; konnect charges a months rent as a re-letting fee $4,000 at our current rent, and they get paid their monthly management fees whether the house is vacant or not.

The sheer lack of professionalism, zero accountability, and greed shown by this agency is neither new, or unexpected, but their determination to screw over both the owners, and tenants ensure they stand out as a poor choice all around.

one_star_reviews.text:
Our family loves the Sushi Train chain, so when we visited the Waterloo "Mini Stop" location, we expected the familiar conveyor belt experience, just in a smaller footprint. It turned out to be nothing like a Sushi Train.

The place is microscopic, with only three tables, and on a busy Sunday evening, there was literally ONE person working.

The single star I’m leaving is purely for the heroic efforts of the poor girl working there. She was doing everything by herself: taking orders at the till, running back into the kitchen to make the sushi, and dealing with a constant stream of Uber Eats drivers, rolling sushi like crazy. Naturally, the service suffers - it is completely unreasonable to expect one person to handle all of that during a weekend rush.

The venue also has no customer toilet, which isn't a huge deal for us, but I couldn't help worrying about the employee. What is she supposed to do if she needs to use the restroom? Leave the whole store unattended and run to find one nearby?
It feels like a total lack of respect for both the staff and the customers.

As for the food, the sushi was fresh and tasty, but you could tell it was prepared in a massive hurry because it was falling apart. I honestly don't hold that against her at all out of sheer empathy for what she was put through, she was running around non-stop and still managed to stay polite and friendly.
I really hope this was just an unforeseen force majeure and she isn't normally left to run the entire shop alone.

Finally, management should really remove "Train" from the name of this location. The whole point of a Sushi Train is being able to sit down and immediately grab plates off the belt. Here, you have to order and wait while a single overwhelmed employee works up a sweat trying to roll everything from scratch.

one_star_reviews.text:
Today I was in a rush to get home and pick up my dog who needed to urgently attend the vet.

As such, I was quite stressed and worried, trying to get to my home as fast as I could. When I got to my street, I saw there were works being done and a road closed sign, right outside my house. At the time I hadn’t seen how far down the street was closed, and obviously needed to know how to access my house. Rather than block a main road, I pulled into my street by a single car length right beside the road closed sign. I wound down my window and asked how I can access my house.

The employee who engaged with me was simply standing by a machine with their hands in their pocket looking off into space. Not wanting to drive further into the closed road, I yelled to get their attention and asked how I can access my house.

The response I was met with was anything but helpful, or at all curious what I was asking and how they could help - something I’d expect is part of the job description as a traffic manager.

Instead, I was met with an aggressive argumentative tone, told the road was closed, and told I had ignored the signs to go around the block. It seemed the aim was not to help, whilst maintaining safety, but to assert their control and dominance over the situation.

From where I was sitting, I was unclear whether going around the block would even solve the issue since it looked like the blocked area included the front of my house.

As there was a sense of urgency in my situation, I simply pointed and said “how do I get to that house?”

Instead of listening, or making any genuine attempt to help me, I was again told I had broken the rules, ignored signs and that under no circumstances could I do anything but reverse out immediately.

Now I accept there may have been a sign on where to detour, being in a rush with a single focus to get my dog since time was of the essence, I had not noticed it. I have no reason to think the employee lied, so I am willing to accept it was there.

However, had I seen it, I don’t believe it would have provided information on whether I could access the specific house I urgently needed to, so in either case, I needed to ask the staff for help.

When it was clear that help was never going to come, and the aggressive employee was solely focused on using their powers of telepathy to tell me I’d seen things I hadn’t, and ignored things I hadn’t, and scold me for it. which even if I had seen wouldn’t have helped me or avoided the need to ask the question, I decided to back out and try my luck to see if I’d be able to get my dog by going the other way.

As I begun turning the car around, I would down my window and asked if I could have the employees name and their employers name, which they refused multiple times and asking why I wanted it. I said it was so I could call their employer and explain the situation, such that g eh at least have the chance to do better next time, provide additional training, and avoid someone else having the same experience. Clearly believing their behaviour was not something they wanted discussed with their employer, they repeatedly told me “it doesn’t matter”. Upon leaving I did see a vehicle parked a few meters away with a contra flow traffic management logo on it.

My question to contra flow is this, does this feedback matter to you? Do you think the opportunity to take feedback on board and implement solutions such that members of the public have more pleasant experiences with your staff is important and valuable to you as a business? Or was the employee speaking for the organisation when they dismissed my request to provide this feedback entirely?

I would appreciate a response to this by the company, if it does in fact matter to them.

If it isn’t, and falls on deaf ears, I’m sure it will be of interest to the council and western power along with any additional feedback from my neighbours about any of their own experiences.  Though I’d much rather see the company take it as an opportunity to learn and improve, as we all make mistakes..

We find this approach completely unacceptable, misleading and deceptive. Their customer service was no better. Businesses should be transparent about their pricing, obtain agreement to costs before undertaking work, and invoice only for services and equipment actually provided. one_star_reviews.text:
I called after seeing the service advertised as somewhere workers could obtain legal advice and guidance about a WorkCover matter.

I was not expecting anyone to immediately agree to represent me. I was seeking exactly what the service appeared to offer: professional guidance about my legal position, what my next steps should be, and how to respond to an urgent preliminary decision.

Instead, after only a very brief discussion, the lawyer said he was not really sure what advice he could give me and then said he was not interested in acting. When I asked what information he would need, or what the next steps would be, he reiterated that he did not want to be involved and ended the call abruptly.

I have no issue with a lawyer deciding not to take on a matter. Firms are entitled to make that decision.

What I found unacceptable was that, once he decided he was not interested in acting, there appeared to be no interest in providing even basic guidance about the situation I had called about, despite that being the reason I contacted the service in the first place - as advertised on their website.

The interaction felt less like a legal advice service and more like a screening call to determine whether my matter was one the firm wanted to take on. Once the answer was no, the conversation ended.

For someone already dealing with a stressful workers’ compensation issue and seeking urgent guidance, I found the experience abrupt, dismissive and deeply discouraging.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend this service to someone looking for practical legal guidance about a WorkCover matter - or, given their general attitude - any matter at all.

I would like to provide feedback regarding my recent experience with the customer service at the NOVO DFO store. Unfortunately, I found the experience very disappointing and frustrating.
I had contacted the Belmont NOVO store regarding the Ivanka heels in size 6. Aisyah kindly confirmed that the DFO store had the shoes available and assured me that a pair would be put aside for me under my name. Based on this confirmation, I travelled to the DFO store specifically to purchase the shoes.
When I arrived, I spoke with Summer and explained that I was there to collect the Ivanka heels that had been placed on hold for me. Summer located the box and brought it to the counter, but the box contained only the left shoe. She advised me that she would locate the right shoe.
After approximately 10 minutes, Summer returned and asked me to wait a few more minutes as Uthara, the staff member who had apparently put the other shoe away, was returning from lunch.
When Uthara returned, she was unable to locate the right shoe. She spent some time walking back and forth but ultimately could not find it. I was extremely disappointed because I had travelled to the store based on the assurance from the Belmont store that the complete pair had been put aside for me.
I understand that mistakes can happen; however, I was particularly disappointed by the lack of urgency and attention given to resolving the issue. If a product has been specifically placed on hold for a customer, I believe staff should ensure that the complete pair is safely located and available before asking the customer to travel to the store.
This experience was inconvenient and left me feeling that my time as a customer was not valued. I would appreciate it if this matter could be reviewed with the DFO store team and appropriate steps taken to improve communication, product handling and customer service.

⭐ 1-Star Review — Very Disappointing Experience
I visited El Jannah Bayswater with my family on Friday, 14 August, around 8pm, and unfortunately, the experience was extremely disappointing.
We were told that no burgers, fried chicken, or any fried chicken items were available because they had run out — even the kids’ meals were unavailable. The only option offered was charcoal chicken. What made it more frustrating was seeing the shelves full of charcoal chicken, which appeared to have been sitting there for some time. It felt as though the priority was simply to sell what was already prepared rather than provide customers with a proper dining experience.
The staff were unwelcoming, rude and unprofessional, with no greeting or basic customer service. I travelled around 25 km to Bayswater, expecting the quality of service I have experienced at other El Jannah locations, but unfortunately, this visit was a huge let-down.
This is not the first time I've been disappointed. Last summer, the dine-in area was extremely cold and uncomfortable, even though we were dressed for summer. When I politely asked a team member if the temperature could be adjusted, the response was rude and I was simply told, “We can't change the temperature.” There seemed to be very little concern for customer comfort.
What makes the contrast even more disappointing is that on the same night, Ferntree Gully staff were able to accommodate my family even though we arrived around 9pm. The team there was welcoming, helpful and professional — exactly what customer service should look like.
Unfortunately, El Jannah Bayswater needs a serious improvement in staff attitude, customer service and dine-in experience. After travelling such a long distance with my family, I left feeling very disappointed.
Not recommended. I hope management takes this feedback seriously and addresses these issues.

one_star_reviews.text:
If I could give 0 stars, I would.

I saw Dr Ben Stephens a few years ago for endometriosis surgery. A few month before my surgery, I had a scan at Omni Sydney which had confirmed endometriosis. Despite this, when Dr Stephens performed my surgery, I was told he found absolutely nothing.

At my post-operative appointment, I was told that I should see a therapist because I was apparently “just a sensitive girl” and that if someone pinched me, I would feel it more than a “normal person.”

I knew in my heart that something was wrong and that my pain was real. I refused to accept that explanation and sought a second opinion from another doctor.

Only around 8 months later, I had another surgery with a different doctor. This doctor found endometriosis, adenomyosis and interstitial cystitis!!!!!????

I reported my experience to the hospital immediately after my second doctor confirmed these diagnoses. I remember being absolutely devastated, crying and sobbing because I had allowed myself to believe that maybe there really was nothing wrong with me. However so relieved that I actually found a doctor that listened and believed me along with having the skills to find these diagnoses.

This experience had a huge impact on my mental health and delayed me getting the diagnosis and treatment I needed to manage my pain. I can’t express how much Ben Stephens has ruined how I am now during appointments or surgery now

I break down at every appointment now so scared another doctor will say these same things he said to me. I actually lost my job at the time straight after surgery with him because I had to take extended leave because of how bad my mental health was after him. On top of crippling pain…

I am sharing my experience because I genuinely hope no other woman has to go through what I did. Women deserve to be listened to, taken seriously and have their pain investigated properly — especially when there is already evidence suggesting something is wrong.

Extremely disappointing experience.

They were helpful when it came to getting me to purchase the tiles. Unfortunately, that level of customer service seemed to disappear the moment the sale was complete.

All I asked was for the tiles to be split across two pallets instead of one. I made this request immediately after purchasing, specifically because I needed to be able to unload the tiles safely and reasonably when I collected them.

It was such a simple request, but apparently too much to ask.

Instead, the entire load was left on one pallet, making collection and unloading unnecessarily difficult. This wasn’t some unreasonable last-minute demand, it was a very straightforward request made in advance that could have easily been accommodated while the order was being prepared.

What is most frustrating is the contrast in service. Before the purchase, extremely helpful. After the purchase, apparently splitting a load across two pallets was too much effort.

For a business selling heavy building materials, you would think there would be some basic consideration for how an actual customer is expected to collect and unload their purchase.

Very helpful when they wanted my money. Not so helpful afterwards.

On 21/08, they finally said my car is ready for collection. Upon collection, they told me nothing about the vehicle being damaged during the repair. When I raised the issue of my windscreen having a big crack on it, the staff said they saw it but wasn't sure what to do with it or whether it was from before. They had insurance photos taken prior to the repair. There is no reason for them to not know this crack had appeared during the repair process. Anyways, no apology was given and they talked about how I had signed the forms already so it's somehow also my fault, even though I haven't even moved my car yet.

My sincere advice: Do not trust this repairer. Do not let this happen to you.

one_star_reviews.text:
Dear Eatons Hill Tavern Management,

I am writing to formally complain about the way our group was treated at Eatons Hill Tavern today.

Our group attended from approximately 3:00–4:00 pm until around 8:30 pm. While this was not formally booked as a 50th birthday party, we were a group of family and friends there to celebrate a friend's 50th birthday. During the afternoon and evening, we spent approximately $1,000–$2,000 at the venue.

The evening was going well until one of our friends ordered a pint of Guinness but was served a schooner. When he requested the pint he had originally ordered, the barmaid told him that the schooner was all they could provide. The staff member's attitude towards our group was uncooperative and negative, and we felt our reasonable request was handled unnecessarily poorly.

Shortly afterwards, security approached our friend and told him he had to leave. We were extremely surprised by this as, from our perspective, he was in no way intoxicated or behaving inappropriately.

When we attempted to discuss the situation with security and staff, we were then told that our entire group was cut off and would not be served any further drinks.

We understand that the venue has responsibilities regarding responsible service of alcohol, and we respect that staff and security have a job to do. However, we strongly disagree with how this situation was handled. There had been no prior indication that our group was causing any issues, and we believe the matter could have been dealt with professionally without escalating to this point.

I am also particularly disappointed because this is not the first time I have experienced or witnessed a situation where our group has spent considerable money at Eatons Hill Tavern and then been treated in this manner.

As a local and patron of the venue, I find this extremely disappointing. We came to enjoy an afternoon and celebrate a friend's 50th birthday, and instead the evening ended with our group feeling unwelcome after spending a substantial amount of money at the venue.

I would appreciate management reviewing the incident and providing an explanation as to:

Why our friend was refused the pint of Guinness he ordered.
Why he was subsequently asked to leave.
Why our entire group was cut off.
What grounds there were for determining that he was intoxicated or required to leave.
Why the situation was handled in this manner by the staff and security.

I would appreciate a response from management and hope this matter is taken seriously.

Regards,

Chris

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointed, would not recommend.

I booked my car in for 12pm because I had a birthday to attend at 2pm. Their website stated the service would take approximately 75 minutes, so I booked based on that timeframe and expected my car to be ready around 1:15pm.

When I arrived, I was told it would actually take around 2 hours. I had already paid, so at that point after having driven all that way I didn’t have much choice but to leave the car with them.

I came back down at 1:50pm and was told they only had about 10 minutes left and that it was basically just the outside that needed finishing. That turned out not to be true. They were only just properly starting on my car, the mats weren’t even taken out to be pressure washed until around 1:55pm. When they got put back in the car the mats were still dripping wet. I had to ask one of the guys to please dry them but even then it was just a slight wipe with a cloth.

In the end, they had four people rushing to finish the car and I didn’t get it back until around 2:15pm. I had waited over two hours, yet from what I could see, less than 30 minutes was actually spent cleaning the car.

I paid $95 for what ultimately felt like a very rushed job. Even worse, I noticed marks/abrasions on the car afterwards that I know were not there beforehand. When I raised it with them, I was simply told the car was already like that, which I strongly disagree with. I’m not sure what they use to wipe but it’s really abrasive.

Had I known from the beginning that they couldn’t complete the service within the advertised timeframe, I would have gone elsewhere.

For $95, I expected much better service, communication and far better care of my vehicle.Not the rushed 25min job that was completed. Unfortunately, based on my experience, I would not return or recommend them. Save your money and take your car somewhere else. I wish I’d read and listened to the reviews. So disappointed.

Unfortunately, I was extremely disappointed with my experience at this clinic.

I arrived on time for my appointment and was left waiting in the waiting area for over an hour. The wait was so long that I actually fell asleep on the couch. Considering I live only two minutes away, I would have really appreciated a phone call or even some communication to let me know the doctor was running significantly behind rather than being left waiting for that amount of time.

I also left the appointment feeling disappointed and without the clarity or answers I had expected from the consultation. Some aspects of the assessment left me feeling confused rather than supported, particularly as I had attended seeking professional guidance and expected things to be explained and explored more thoroughly.

The follow-up afterwards was even more frustrating. Important information from my appointment was supposed to be sent to my GP, however when I attended my GP appointment, nothing had been received. Both my GP and I contacted the clinic and were told it would be sent through.

However, when I returned to my GP two days later, the information STILL had not been received. My GP and I then had to contact the clinic again to have it sent through.

For a service dealing with people's mental health and wellbeing, I expected much better organisation, communication and follow-up. Having to repeatedly chase important information between the clinic and my GP added unnecessary stress to an already frustrating experience.

Unfortunately, based on my experience, I would not recommend this clinic.

My son and I were with Future Focus (i-Coordinate) only a few months ago, and unfortunately, our experience was extremely disappointing.

Thousands of dollars were invoiced for support coordination, yet very little was actually done to support my son. His plan review was supposed to be processed months ago, well before he finished Year 12, so there could be a proper plan in place for his transition into the future. Despite this, the coordinator failed to get the process underway.

My son is now about to finish school and is left without a proper plan for what happens next. His behaviour therapist ultimately had to step in and submit the plan review because we were getting nowhere with the support coordinators.

From our experience, there was a lot of billing but very little meaningful support or action when it was actually needed.

If you genuinely need proactive and reliable support coordination, based on our experience, I would recommend looking elsewhere. Unfortunately, I cannot understand the number of positive reviews given the experience we had and can only assume they have been paid reviews.

Very disappointing, especially when the consequences of poor support coordination can have such a significant impact on a young person’s future.

English version

We had a very disappointing experience at this car wash. We took our car there to be washed and, after the service, we noticed that the reverse camera was damaged and the screen was showing a completely distorted image.

We spoke to the administrator to ask if they could help us or at least look into what had happened. We understand that, without direct evidence, they could not confirm that the damage happened while the car was there. However, the way we were treated was completely unacceptable. He was very rude and spoke to us in an aggressive and disrespectful tone.

At one point, he even asked if we spoke Spanish, and from that moment his attitude towards us became even worse. Speaking another language should never be a reason to treat customers differently.

We didn’t expect them to accept responsibility without evidence, but we did expect empathy, professionalism and a genuine effort to help. A business that handles customers’ cars should also have appropriate insurance or procedures in place to deal with possible damage that may occur while a vehicle is in their care.

The way this situation was handled was what disappointed us the most. We simply wanted to be heard and treated with respect, but unfortunately, that was not our experience.

We will not be returning.

My experience with Evolved Hair has been extremely disappointing, particularly the complete lack of communication once things went wrong.

My original hair transplant did not achieve the result I was expecting, and Evolved agreed to perform a corrective procedure at no charge. I was given a date for the correction, only for it to be cancelled. Another corrective procedure was then booked and confirmed for September.

In the weeks leading up to it, I repeatedly called, emailed and messaged trying to get the blood-test referral and information I had been told would be sent to me. Calls went unanswered, messages weren't returned and I was constantly the one having to chase them.

Despite all of this, I received an automated appointment reminder on the morning of the procedure. I tried calling again around my appointment time and still couldn't get anyone to answer.

This has been the pattern throughout my experience: promises that things will be organised, dates being booked, then little or no communication and me having to continually chase for answers.

For something as personal and significant as a hair transplant, I expected considerably better patient care and communication.

This review is based entirely on my personal experience and the communications and records I have retained

one_star_reviews.text:
Luke Bevans uses social media content to promote and sell records, and in one of these videos he was promoting the new Miss Kaninna record on yellow vinyl as an exclusive release. A big part of that exclusivity was the inclusion of an obi strip (a flat piece of cardboard wrapped around the vinyl sleeve) and the fact that each copy was hand numbered.

What actually arrived was a record with no obi strip. Instead, there was a very small hype sticker attached to the plastic shrink wrap around the record. For many collectors, that plastic is removed and discarded, meaning the “hand numbered” element being advertised effectively disappears with it.

As a record collector who specifically collects limited pressings and obi strips, I consider this to be misleading advertising, and I was extremely disappointed with the purchase.

When I commented on the promotional video, Luke Bevans responded by saying, “We worked with the label to make a hand numbered sticker instead.” What was missing was any apology or acknowledgement that the product being advertised was different from what customers actually received.

I was then told that if I wasn’t happy, I could send the record back. The way this was communicated came across as quite condescending, particularly given that I was simply raising a legitimate concern about a product that had been advertised with an obi strip but arrived without one.

After more than 10 years of collecting records, this is the first time I have purchased a record specifically advertised as including an obi strip that has arrived without one. Unfortunately, the experience has been made considerably worse by the way the issue was handled.

Luke, make it right. You advised that an obi strip could be sent to me , so send one.

Until then, I’ll be taking my business elsewhere and encouraging other collectors to carefully consider what they are actually receiving before purchasing from this label. I will also be spreading the word amongst the community to boycott. Very disappointed
